A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GRW dataset and co-speech gesture recognition work. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A-E are readable and can be matched across revisions and renumbering.

before.justification: Sections 5 and 7 report original dataset analyses, trained-model evaluations, generalization experiments, and ablations, including Tables 4-7.

after.justification: Sections 5 and 7 retain original empirical analyses and experiments, with revised results in Tables 5-8 and added confusion matrices in Figure 8.

M1.justification: Section 6.3 replaces temporal mean pooling with pooling weighted by predicted localization probabilities for word recognition. Appendix Table 8 in v1 versus Table 9 in v2 also changes the reported recognition/localization hidden width from 512 to 768. These refine the existing architecture; the backbone, semantic classifier, losses, and two-stage training approach remain.

E1.justification: GRW's reported vocabulary expands from 150 to 155 words. The English MultiVSR-derived domain, three gesture tasks, 100-word recognition test coverage, unseen-word evaluation, and AVS-Spot evaluation remain. Revised clip and identity counts do not independently establish a new domain or population.

E2.justification: Both principal comparison tables add Sapiens, Intern-VL, and Qwen3-VL, and replace Gemini-3 with Gemini-3.5, substantially broadening the comparator set. Clip4Clip, GestSync, JEGAL, and SemanticMoments remain; SemanticMoments is now labeled SemMomDinov3 with its DINOv3 features specified.

E3.justification: Table 2 revises classifier training clips from 152,688 to 135,503, clean recognition training clips from 15,473 to 15,340, and pretraining clips from 61,141 to 67,214. The recognition model's reported width increases to 768, and Section 7.1 adds recall evaluation at high confidence. Reported test-set sizes, core metrics, context-length settings, and optimization schedules remain.

E4.justification: New Figure 8 compares the proposed model's and Gemini's confusion matrices, extending the existing qualitative error analysis. Appendix E replaces the peak/raise failure example with round/global while retaining little/tiny. The context-length and pretraining ablation questions remain; new Table 4 supplements the existing timing analysis with selected-word duration means.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Predictive confidence thresholds and descriptive duration distributions already appear in v1; added recall results do not introduce statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Principal results are broadly revised: proposed-model classification accuracy changes from 70.25% to 75.83%, recognition Acc@1 from 18.57% to 18.35%, and localization mIoU from 0.6643 to 0.6731. AVS-Spot accuracy changes from 79.8% to 77.3%, with JEGAL remaining at 63.6%. Dataset statistics, ablation scores, and qualitative examples also change, alongside new baseline and recall results. Revised training data and model settings prevent interpreting these as controlled performance gains.

T1.justification: The task definitions and combined classification/localization loss remain mathematically equivalent. Changes from T or l to Q standardize notation rather than introduce new theory. Neither version contains new theorems, proofs, or substantive theoretical derivations.

C1.justification: The dataset contribution's stated scale changes from 156,688 clips and 12,010 identities to 139,503 clips and 37,409 identities, with 150 versus 155 words. The central claims about the GRW benchmark, three gesture tasks, temporal-context benefits, and superiority over comparison methods remain.

C2.justification: Section 7.1 newly qualifies high-confidence gesture mining with its low recall: 35% on GRW and 31.3% on unseen words. V1 emphasized clean mining without reporting this cost. The public-discourse and English-language limitations, and the interpretation of semantically ambiguous recognition errors, already appeared in v1.

D1.justification: V2 reports public availability of the dataset, annotations, and trained models; Appendix C.2 changes code/model release from planned to completed. It newly specifies 10 unseen words and 201 positive clips within the 500-clip evaluation, and DINOv3 features for SemanticMoments. Most annotation, preprocessing, training, and prompt documentation is retained.

R1.justification: Related work adds SocialGesture, co-speech segmentation and dialogue-representation studies, SemGes, and SemConFlow. Section 5.2 links timing findings to additional prior studies, and new baselines receive citations. These extend the research context while retaining the main positioning around word-grounded gestures in unconstrained video.

P1.justification: The abstract is rewritten, related-work and results passages receive limited expansions, and terminology, notation, and acknowledgements are revised. The main section sequence and Appendix A-E structure remain, with much explanatory prose unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 6 is substantially redrawn, a duration table and paired confusion matrices are added, and baseline tables gain rows. Dataset illustrations, successful predictions, and appendix failure examples are refreshed. Figure 5 removes the exact-boundary-overlap bar, and appendix typography and figure placement change. These constitute substantial visual revisions beyond score updates and renumbering.

improvement.justification: Broader baseline comparisons, added confusion matrices, and explicit reporting of the recall cost of high-confidence mining make v2's empirical evidence more informative. The reported resource release also improves reproducibility information. These benefits are tempered by new reporting inconsistencies: Table 1 gives 173 hours versus 153.67 in Table 2, and Table 9 retains a 512-dimensional input within the revised 768-dimensional recognition block. The net improvement is limited rather than established by higher reported scores.
